## The Story Today

A new friction point has emerged over the "ownership" of the Strait of Hormuz. While Oman has proposed a fee plan to manage the waterway ([The New York Times](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimgFBVV95cUxQWU5DMS1mNG9RNm8yTTkzclFNMWVNRmtCNmI0M1kxdEF4RkdrTlJBV1lCeTFpUGVFcDVRRzdoSDZBYkJYbWRKaEJOWTBwREZUS3ZEMFlCYWU3N2F3eGREWHJBM0l4Q09lLWItS3VvenpzUjlJbTAyc0pzNi1zaVNKS1FwTTF3MUkxX2FTX1k0LUcyTm4xMkxscmd3), 2026-06-30), Tehran is actively competing with Muscat to remain the primary decision-maker for the strait ([The Guardian](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMioAFBVV95cUxOMHVrNEpxbVZsNjNPV0tUeWxySVZxOE9DWUthVS0tVF9HQWJJcXpKdWdSNDlLSmY2bjZZQlJYaTNqMnhiaUF2c1VnY0VkNVNBMmpjZEZIRXRDd0VqTUZUcUZ2YUJLTUUxZXFiVEJrWVdLQ1lxZGcwZTd6S0JOTFluRjJFYmJQc3hIMXE5UndDUldXdC1rb2lZeU9vQVF6TVFp), 2026-06-30). This suggests that even as a broader peace deal is pursued, regional control over strategic chokepoints remains a zero-sum game.

The EU is maintaining a hard line on sanctions despite the momentum of the US-Iran MoU. The EU will not lift key sanctions until a formal nuclear deal is finalized ([Al Jazeera](https://news.google.), 2026-06-19). This creates a tiered sanctions environment where US relief may precede European relief, potentially complicating the "final deal" Tehran expects before allowing full IAEA access ([NPR](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMidEFVX3lxTE5ZekVWT180T1ZmWHUwN1lCRXNLLVhSbWw0VTUwZ2pRUmdGaGV6R2UtcUZWd0Z3R2txNVdzanVwaGx4VFNLclhPVm9uSEI2SmtEb3lFMzcwUFV4TmhGVmFkRDVkOE5fdXhtelJWWTRZMHd0bGlv), 2026-06-24).

The IAEA remains the primary point of verification tension. While the IAEA head claims the current deal grants access to nuclear sites ([Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxQbklORW1hNXYwX1pxRFpuTlVTZ0xTZUJOVXdXcUdScUpoQm1fUGx3NUVMZGh4S0hYelhlSEdUd1dDTzUydU9xWW5kWDZxMnd2U3prZklQSXZjRk1aQ2J2OEt5Wkl4Tm1kaktRRDhxdGJlZjJuWF9VNC1jSkhpT2tqajdWbXNYVUhqVTJZZGdCSnNBV0YwOTRCWVhrWnFHdDdkTm9aTkVTOFhfb1BDM0RBaFFn), 2026-06-26), he continues to emphasize that Iran is "duty bound" to cooperate ([朝日新聞](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiVkFVX3lxTE50aDVpZ0FoV2hVci11bm9GQjFxckVZVGlCTjB6MXl0ZVBpcV9S1S3d4ZHJhZ0ZtWTk2UFZUQ25pYjZtV2lmZmxkTTBrMm1sdk9iSV9n), 2026-06-29). The gap between "granted access" and "actual verification" is where the deal is most fragile.
